questions.question: A transfer debits Account A, then the credit to Account B fails. Which property should ensure neither balance changes?
options: Atomicity
Consistency
Isolation
Durability
questions.explanation: Atomicity makes the related writes one all-or-nothing unit, so the database rolls the debit back when the credit cannot complete.

questions.question: Which statement best describes consistency in ACID?
options: Every replica sees a write at the same instant
A transaction takes valid data to another valid state
Every request waits for every other request
A committed row is copied to a cache
questions.explanation: ACID consistency is about preserving constraints and business invariants, such as a valid foreign key or a non-negative inventory count.

questions.question: Two shoppers read that one item remains and both submit an order. What is the safest single-statement way to encode the inventory invariant?
options: Read the count from a replica again
UPDATE inventory SET available = available - 1 WHERE sku = ? AND available > 0
Insert an analytics event before the order
Retry both orders until they succeed
questions.explanation: The guarded update checks and changes availability in the same database operation. Its affected-row count tells the application whether the reservation succeeded.

questions.question: Why must an application be ready to retry a serializable transaction?
options: Serializable transactions never commit
The database may abort one transaction to preserve a serial outcome
Durability is disabled at this level
Constraints cannot be used with serializable isolation
questions.explanation: To make concurrent work equivalent to a serial order, a database may detect a conflict and abort one transaction. A safe, idempotent retry can then re-run it.

questions.question: What does durability promise after a database has acknowledged COMMIT?
options: The result can survive recovery from a crash
No query will ever be slow
All future transactions are isolated
The result is already in every downstream service
questions.explanation: Durability means the acknowledged committed state is recoverable after failures, commonly through logs, flushes, replication, and recovery procedures.

questions.question: Why place a notification in a transactional outbox instead of calling the notification service inside the order transaction?
options: It makes the remote call part of the SQL rollback
It records the intent with the order, then delivers it asynchronously after commit
It removes the need for idempotency
It guarantees the notification is shown before the order exists
questions.explanation: The outbox row commits atomically with the business record. A separate worker can retry delivery without holding database locks during a network call.
